title: Predictors of Health-Related QOL in Adults With CLL or Small Lymphocytic Lymphoma
official: Predictors of Health-Related Quality of Life in Adults With Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia or Small Lymphocytic Lymphoma
summary: The study aims to improve our understanding of how quality of life, fatigue, and symptoms change over 2 years when participants are treated for chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma. We will compare two types of treatment to help future patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma know what to anticipate.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* All patients with pathology-confirmed diagnoses of CLL who are within seven days of starting treatment with a BTKi +/- an anti-CD 20 monoclonal antibody or BCL2i with Obinutuzumab treatment will be included.
* Subjects must be able to read and speak English or Spanish at the 8th grade level.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients with dementia, traumatic brain injury, or individuals with central nervous system involvement of their leukemia will be excluded from study participation.
sponsor: H. Lee Moffitt Cancer Center and Research Institute
